summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted for shortness of breath and chest tightness. Imaging and clinical findings indicated pulmonary edema due to volume overload, despite her being below her usual weight. She was treated with intravenous Lasix, achieving a 3-liter negative fluid balance, and her symptoms resolved. Her carvedilol dose was increased to 12.5 mg twice daily for better heart function control, while lisinopril was held due to elevated creatinine. Hyperkalemia was managed with Kayexalate and dietary counseling. Her transplant medications were continued without change, and she was discharged home with instructions on fluid and sodium restriction, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up lab work.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
